Parse the JSON event stream: the review text is the concatenated assistant text parts; token usage (input, cached input, output, reasoning) and cost are summed from the [path redacted] events. a run that ends `deadline-exceeded` (worker wall or validation-queue wait) with a committed candidate is recorded as a preserved candidate that `delegate-publish --revalidate <run-dir>` can validate and publish, instead of being lost. - At the deadline, if the worktree has exactly one new commit over the recorded base and the tree is clean, record that commit as the run's candidate (candidate SHA in [path redacted], preserved ref via the existing `preserve_candidate`, [path redacted]:118-160), with the terminal state still `deadline-exceeded` and a one-line `candidate preserved for revalidation` note in run.log. A dirty tree or zero or several new commits: no candidate, exactly as today. - `delegate-publish --revalidate <run-dir>` accepts such a run: it runs the normal scope, identity and full validation gates on that exact commit and publishes it the normal way (draft PR, or push onto the base PR branch for a work run on an open PR). Every gate stays mandatory; nothing is published without validation passing. - The deadline itself stays a failure: a run that is never revalidated still reads `deadline-exceeded` in delegate-status. - Tests (offline, fake adapter): a worker that commits then overruns the wall → candidate recorded; revalidate publishes it; a dirty tree or two commits → no candidate and revalidate refuses with a reason; each guard fails its test when removed. Spans lib, bin and tests because the deadline path, the publish command and their tests are one behavior.

every `[path redacted]` run ends with a machine-checked verdict that the launcher records and posts on the reviewed PR. - The review prompt the launcher builds tells the reviewer that its final line must be exactly `APPROVED for merge` or `REQUEST CHANGES`, overriding the worker report format's ending ([path redacted]). - After a review run, the launcher reads the reviewer's final message: the last non-empty line must be one of the two verdicts. Record `review_verdict` (approved / changes / missing) and the reviewed head SHA in [path redacted]. - Post the reviewer's final message as one PR comment, headed with the verdict, the model and the exact head SHA, unless `--no-post` is given. A missing verdict is posted as "no verdict" and the run's state says so (never a silent approval). Posting failures are recorded and reported, not fatal to the recorded verdict. - Tests (offline, fake gh): approved, changes and missing verdicts are recorded; the comment carries head SHA and verdict; `--no-post` posts nothing; each guard fails its test when removed.

the validation queue admits a validation only when its memory weight fits the host's validation memory budget, in addition to the existing slot count. - repos.conf: per-repo `validation_memory_gb` (default 1.5) and host `validation_memory_budget_gb` (default: unset = today's behavior, count slots only). Read and validated with the other queue keys ([path redacted]:190-222); a bad value refuses with a clear message. - Admission (the [path redacted] transaction, [path redacted]:284-348): with a budget set, admit only when the sum of admitted weights plus this one is within the budget; a validation heavier than the whole budget still runs alone rather than waiting forever. Record the weight in the slot entry and in [path redacted]. - Waiting for memory is visible: the queue position message says it waits for memory (used / budget GB). - Tests (offline): two 2 GB validations under a 3 GB budget run one at a time; under 4 GB both run; an over-budget one runs alone; unset budget keeps count-only behavior; each guard fails its test when removed.

when a worker turn or run ends, every process it started is gone, including ones that left the worker's process group. - At spawn, record the worker's pid and start time. At the end of each worker turn and of the run, walk the process table for descendants of the worker (parent chain, pid + start time to avoid pid reuse) plus any process whose working directory is inside the run's worktree, and signal them TERM, wait a bounded grace period, then KILL. Never signal a process that is not a descendant or not inside the worktree. - Record every reaped process (pid, command, how it was matched, signal used) in [path redacted] and one summary line in run.log. A process that survives KILL is reported and makes the run say so (no silent pass). - bash 3.2 and Linux: use `ps -axo pid=,ppid=,lstart=,command=` style portable output; macOS has no /proc. - Tests (offline, fake adapter): a worker that starts a `setsid`/new-group sleeper → it is reaped and recorded; an unrelated process with the same command is untouched; a reused pid with a different start time is untouched; each guard fails its test when removed.

validations that are known to be fast run in a separate small fast-lane pool instead of waiting behind slow ones. - repos.conf: per-repo `validation_fast = true` (owner-declared), and a host `validation_fast_slots` (default 2). It still runs the exact head with every gate unchanged. - It is bounded by `validation_fast_max_seconds` x 4: if it runs longer, it is stopped and requeued in the normal pool (recorded in run.log), and the repo's measured history is updated so it stops qualifying. - Record `validation_lane` ([path redacted]) and the duration in [path redacted]. - Tests (offline): a declared-fast repo bypasses a full normal pool; measured-fast qualifies after 3 short runs; an overrunning fast validation is requeued; non-fast repos never use the fast lane; each guard fails its test when removed.
